content.text:
I've checked the brief line by line against the release. Summary of what I found:

**Key facts:** Seven of ten are stated correctly. Three are absent — the brief never mentions commercial remaining performance obligation (+84% to $678 billion), capital expenditures (additions to property and equipment of $35,802 million in the quarter vs. $17,079 million), or the discrete items versus the April 29, 2026 guidance (including the $3.2 billion Anthropic gain and the $0.27 net EPS benefit). Those are material omissions for an investment committee: the RPO figure is the release's forward-demand signal, the capex more than doubled year over year, and without the $0.27 discrete benefit a reader cannot tell how much of the EPS beat was operational.

**Claims:** Everything the brief does assert checks out against the release, with one exception — the attribution of Productivity and Business Processes growth to Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud and LinkedIn. The release lists those as highlights but never identifies them as drivers, and the brief omits Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud (+14% reported, +16% adjusted), which is the much larger component of that segment. The GAAP/non-GAAP labelling throughout the brief is handled correctly, including the net income and EPS pairs.

facts.evidence: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, was $90.0 billion, an increase of 18% (17% in constant currency).
Diluted earnings per share for the quarter was $4.81 on a GAAP basis (up 32%)
Diluted earnings per share for the quarter was ... $4.74 on a non-GAAP basis (up 23%). ... Monitor the impact of investments in OpenAI
Intelligent Cloud revenue was $39.3 billion (up 32% reported, 31% in constant currency), with Azure and other cloud services revenue increasing 43%.
Operating income for the quarter was $40.6 billion, an increase of 18%.
Microsoft Cloud revenue for the quarter was $59.3 billion, an increase of 27%.
More Personal Computing revenue decreased 4% (down 5% in constant currency) to $12.9 billion

claims.claim: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $90.0 billion.
Quarterly revenue increased 18% year over year.
Quarterly revenue increased 17% in constant currency.
Operating income for the quarter was $40.6 billion.
Quarterly operating income increased 18% year over year.
Net income for the quarter was $35.8 billion on a GAAP basis, up 31%.
Net income for the quarter was $35.3 billion on a non-GAAP basis, up 22%.
Diluted earnings per share for the quarter was $4.81 on a GAAP basis, up 32%.
Diluted earnings per share for the quarter was $4.74 on a non-GAAP basis, up 23%.
For full fiscal year 2026, revenue was $331.8 billion, up 18%.
For full fiscal year 2026, net income was $133.7 billion on a GAAP basis, up 31%.
Intelligent Cloud revenue was $39.3 billion, up 32% reported and 31% in constant currency.
Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 43%.
Productivity and Business Processes revenue was $37.8 billion, up 14%.
Productivity and Business Processes growth was driven by Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue and LinkedIn revenue.
claims.note: The release lists these only as business highlights and never identifies drivers of segment growth. It also reports Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud revenue up 14% reported (16% adjusted for 2 points of prior-year in-period recognition), a larger component the brief omits, so the causal attribution is the analyst's own inference.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Consumer cloud revenue increased 24% reported and 22% in constant currency.
LinkedIn revenue increased 12% reported and 10% in constant currency.
More Personal Computing revenue was $12.9 billion, down 4% reported and down 5% in constant currency.
XBOX content and services revenue decreased 10%.
Windows OEM and Devices revenue decreased 7%.
Microsoft Cloud revenue for the quarter was $59.3 billion, an increase of 27%.
Microsoft will provide forward-looking guidance in connection with this quarterly earnings announcement on its earnings conference call and webcast.
Total assets as of June 30, 2026 were $758.376 billion, compared with $619.003 billion as of June 30, 2025.
Total cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments were $76.843 billion as of June 30, 2026.
Microsoft returned $10.2 billion to shareholders via dividends and share repurchases in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026.
Investments in OpenAI resulted in a $4.963 billion increase to full-year fiscal 2026 net income.
Microsoft 365 Copilot has reached over 30 million paid seats.
